recs.name: Silverash's Shadow
recs.tag: Protecting one's liege is not the only way for Courier to show loyalty.

lines.x: Sunlight dances off the snow-capped mountains, rendering them immaculately radiant.
The howling wind carries the tolling of bells and the echoes of chanting voices, weaving through the peaks and narrating countless ancient tales.
Here, time seems to have stopped, as if everything has remained unchanged since the dawn of existence.
Hm?
Mm—
Judging from the depth of the footprints, the snow here is deeper than expected.
No doubt from the previous localized snowfall. Given the steep slopes, if the snow keeps accumulating...
I believe the experts that Sir Enciodes hired said there could be heavy snowfall in the next few days.
If that happens...
What is it, sir?
Take a team and measure the depth of the snow, then get an expert to look at the slope gradient...
And assess the risk of avalanche.
Yes, sir.
Then... I'll report to Sir Enciodes once this message has been passed on.
Weiss cannot help but frown at the scene before him.
Soldiers wearing the finest armor and wielding the best weapons have lost all will to fight.
Most lie moaning on the ground. Only a few still have the strength to glare at the tall, blonde woman who put them in this miserable state.
Weiss raises an eyebrow slightly at the sight of the old man beside the woman.
I presume you are not willing to grace us with your presence?
I'm just here to whip these weaklings into shape.
There is no need for banquets.
I simply wish to express my appreciation for your training of Clan Silverash's warriors.
No need.
I'm not training them for Clan Silverash.
And they won't be serving you.
You—
Madam Degenbrecher.
Hm?
Sir Enciodes has a message for you.
And?
He has a meeting, and your presence is required.
Where is he?
Waiting for you at home.
Very well.
That's enough for today. Dismissed.
...*sigh*.
I've heard that she was a stubborn one. Today I got to see for myself.
You should not have come, Mr. Edwin.
Have to hear it with my own ears to give up.
Just as well. I wanted to talk to you too, Weiss. A moment?
...Certainly.
What is it, Mr. Edwin?
I'll cut straight to the chase. What do you think about Degenbrecher, Weiss?
She's very strong. Sir Enciodes is much safer with her around.
You're a smart kid, Weiss. You know that isn't what I'm asking.
You want to know what I think of her presence.
She has taken your place ever since Sir Enciodes brought her back. Do you truly not think anything of it?
What I think is not important. What's important is that Sir Enciodes's work is progressing.
You sound like you don't like her.
I've heard her reputation, a three-time champion somewhere. And it's every bit well deserved, from what I saw today.
But to spend so much money on one person, and putting her in such an important position...
If I may be blunt... Enciodes was shortsighted with this decision.
Pray be careful about your words, Mr. Edwin.
Ever his steadfast defender.
I watched him grow up. He has to call me mister, same as you.
Do you think the others don't think the same way? They're just too afraid to speak their mind.
I'm sure it has occurred to you that Sir Enciodes did this in order to gain a foothold in Victorian high society.
Then why not leave her in Victoria?
Did he forget he already has a bodyguard in Kjerag?
And what would this bodyguard think when he saw her?
As I've said, what I think is not important.
Perhaps that's your outlook. You're a humble boy, after all.
But what of the others?
How much ground did the Paleroches and Browntails take from us in the years that he was abroad?
How many went over to their sides?
Who fought tooth and nail to earn what Silverash has now?
Master Chester, Matterhorn, you, and old-timers like us.
Even if you don't think that way, how many would be envious? Unhappy?
This isn't about Degenbrecher. I've seen my share of proud and capable youngsters.
One or two of her won't do any harm.
But those young people he brought back from Victoria will strip our flesh from our bones.
Sir Enciodes doesn't play favorites.
Of course, he hasn't neglected us.
But is that enough? Why are those fledglings considered our equals and even given better treatment?
Why should we step aside for them, after all that we've given for the clan?
Perhaps Sir Enciodes sees their value.
What value? Like my second son, who believes the future of Kjerag is in his hands just because he learned a few tricks?
Does Sir Enciodes really believe these arrogant fools can contribute to Kjerag's future?
Why are you so certain that I'm on your side, Mr. Edwin?
I watched you and Matterhorn give everything for the clan in the years that Sir Enciodes was away.
Never mind my old friends. I would say this for you two kids.
What does it matter if you go and tell him?
I would say the same to his face, if he was standing in front of me today.
But young people never listen.
You want to make an example of Madam Degenbrecher?
Sir Enciodes, and the young people around him, need to realize that no foreigner can be the master of Kjerag.
The easiest way to deal with a flock of unruly fowlbeasts is to make an example of the one that flies the highest.
One moment.
We finished the survey, sir.
What did the expert say?
Sir, I...
Sir Enciodes trusts him. You can speak frankly.
Yes, sir. The expert says that your assessment is correct, and that the slopes over there are dangerous.
Any further snowfall could potentially cause an avalanche.
...I wish I was wrong.
We were fortunate to find out now. It would have been too late, if not for your experience.
Perhaps.
We should report it to Sir Enciodes, shouldn't we?
...I'll do it. Continue to keep an eye on things.
Yes, sir.
What's on your mind, Weiss?
I understand where you're coming from, Mr. Edwin.
Your concern for the future of Clan Silverash is most touching.
I knew you would understand.
I have an idea.
You heard the report. An avalanche is likely to occur in the near future.
I will ask Sir Enciodes to have Madam Degenbrecher organize a training near where the avalanche is expected to occur.
When it does, we will request assistance.
Who knows what will happen in the chaos?
...A fine plan.
I would have thought it premeditated, had I not heard you talking to your men.
Wait, no, I understand. You've been thinking about this for a while, haven't you?
Yes. The others don't know you, but I do. You're a proud boy, deep down.
You won't just let someone take your place.
Yes, I've been waiting for someone loyal to Silverash like yourself.
The old man did not notice the emphasis that Weiss placed on 'Silverash'.
Sir, as I was delivering the message, I discovered that an avalanche is likely to occur around Moonfang Peak.
How sure are you?
Based on my recent meteorological and geographical studies, 90% sure.
Expert analysis has confirmed the observation.
This is an opportunity.
Yes.
Do as you see fit.
Yes, sir.
I said you didn't need to call me 'sir'.
Old habits die hard.
I may need to borrow Madam Degenbrecher.
Not a problem.
You'll have to convince her yourself, though.
Ha. I'll try.
Oh, I ran into Mr. Edwin today.
Oh? I've heard he's been active. What did he say?
He seems to be in good spirits, and sends you his regards.
Good.
What is it, Weiss? Coming out here was quite the trip for my old bones.
There is something I wish to discuss.
What is it? Have you made arrangements regarding Degenbrecher?
Of course. No need to worry.
Good.
Say, why are there so few people in the village?
Simple.
My men went door to door to persuade the villagers to evacuate.
The stubborn conservatives are the only ones left.
Conservatives? Evacuate?
It would have taken more effort if you were better-informed.
Makes my preparations seem pointless when you just show up like this.
You... you set me up?
Not quite.
Didn't you hear there was going to be an avalanche?
This is the place it's expected to happen.
What did you just say?!
Are you out of your mind, Weiss?!
I expected you to tell Enciodes, but I didn't expect this!
I'm not sure what you mean.
You lured me here and won't let me leave... what do you think I mean?!
You thought I brought you to 'Kjeragandr's turnover' to eliminate you?
What else?! You cold-hearted, ungrateful bastard!
Yes, that's what the people of Kjerag would have thought in the past.
But—
I'll be frank with you, Mr. Edwin.
There are easier ways to kill you, if that's what I intended.
But—
Progress report.
All the buildings near the mountain have been demolished. We have plenty of space to set up a line of defense.
As expected, however, we are meeting resistance from some of the residents who refuse to leave.
The evacuation?
Most of the residents are listening to us and are evacuating. The more stubborn ones refuse to believe us, though.
Leave it to me.
Where are you going, sir?
Requesting Madam Degenbrecher's assistance.
The old noble frantically tries to escape the room, no longer paying attention to what Weiss is saying.
However, Weiss seizes him by the shoulders and pushes his bloated frame toward the warrior.
Take good care of Mr. Edwin while I'm gone.
Yes, sir.
Don't worry, Mr. Edwin. You'll live, at least for today.
I need your help with something, Madam Degenbrecher.
You're out of breath. Something serious?
We believe an avalanche is about to occur near Moonfang Peak, and we need your help.
Do you really need my help?
Of course—
My team has set up defenses, but I need you and your team to help protect the residents who insist on staying.
If I recall correctly, Enciodes has given you and your team quite the power.
You seem too smart to leave such a large gap that would need me to cover.
We're short-handed, after all.
I'm curious. Why go to such lengths for me?
When I was little, I would sometimes run off into the mountains after a fight with Matterhorn.
But I always went back home for dinner, my tail between my legs, when I got hungry,
That was when I learned—
No matter what we do out there during the day, we always return to the same place and eat at the same table at night.
And it would be too awkward to be on bad terms with someone else at that table.
You heard the man.
Get ready to move.
Ma'am, yes, ma'am!
Like master, like servant. You're just like Enciodes.
I'll take that as a compliment.
You just reminded me, though.
Speaking of avalanche...
Say—
Isn't 'madam' a little too distant when we're eating at the same table?
Change it.
Umm...
Well.
I'll leave it to you...
Degenbrecher.
Degenbrecher does not turn around, but neither does she complain.
Ha.
Time to deal with the other problem.
I'm back.
What did Madam Degenbrecher say?
She will help.
Good to hear. The people's opinion of her will change, if they see her help them out.
It's not that she wouldn't. She just needed a chance.
What of Mr. Edwin?
Much calmer. He asked for a cup of tea.
That's the Mr. Edwin I know.
I told you, I would say the same to Sir Enciodes's face.
I was a fool to be deceived by your facade and to believe you could be won over. You've got me—now do as you will.
I went through all this trouble because I know what kind of person you are.
If you'd been anything else, you would have died that day in the mountains.
Hmph. Now I'm curious why you planned all this.
You were setting the stage for Degenbrecher from the beginning?
She'll get there eventually, I'm just helping speed things up.
Why go to such lengths for her?
You thought I would dislike Degenbrecher, because you thought I was like you.
A decade ago, perhaps I'd agree. But I let those feelings go a long time ago.
There are many ways that I can serve Sir Enciodes. Being his bodyguard is not the only way.
And I'm sure he would be disappointed in me if I agreed with you.
Not loathing Degenbrecher is one thing. Why would you help her? Would she even appreciate it?
At first, I only trusted the judgment of Sir Enciodes, who brought her here. And I admit, she was not easy to get along with.
But when you understand that her aloofness is not hostility, only detachment, even confusion...
Then you realize there is no reason to fear her.
You've never seen her standing in the woods, patiently listening to a herder's small talk despite her apparent indifference.
If you had, you would want more people to understand and accept her, as I do.
It will be a good thing for Kjerag, for herself, and for Sir Enciodes, if she is accepted by Kjerag.
As for whether she appreciates my help... that doesn't matter.
Does Enciodes know what you're doing?
Sir Enciodes has to take radical measures to achieve his vision.
Opposition to his methods is expected, but he only has so much time and energy, and he cannot deal with all of it on his own.
I'm simply helping to share the burden where I can.
Whether he knows it or not is equally unimportant.
Follow me, Mr. Edwin.
You will soon learn that Sir Enciodes's vision has long been much more than just the Silverash Clan.
The old noble suddenly thinks that the avalanche does not matter anymore.
Because he sees a vast open expanse where houses once stood.
A dozen or so massive trucks, laden with heavy machinery, are parked across the field. The robotic arms of the machinery transform and interlock—
Coming together to form a wall of steel.
What is—
There is a bit of a story behind this.
I've become quite familiar with the mountains and snow of Kjerag, after years of delivering Sir Enciodes's letters.
When he returned to Kjerag, he authorized me to form an avalanche warning team.
We were able to accurately predict this avalanche with the help of the experts who came back to Kjerag with him.
We can't stop a big avalanche, but we can trigger it before it builds up beyond our capabilities.
That way, we nip large-scale avalanches in the bud, and prevent them from happening.
You're too humble, sir.
Initially, we thought the best we could do was issue avalanche warnings ahead of time; since we didn't have the people or resources to stop them.
Your plan completely changed things.
I just came up with the idea. It's the experts who cracked the complicated math.
Preventing large avalanches?
Yes. You're looking at our line of defense.
It will grow even stronger in the future.
When that day comes, anyone can stand where you stand right now, and watch Kjeragandr's turnover.
But for now, you're the first to be in that best seat.
Watch as it begins.
It begins with a small chunk of snow slipping and falling. As though it were a cue, a low, deep rumble reverberates through the valley.
In an instant, the trickle of snow transforms into a roaring torrent, uprooting trees and sweeping away boulders.
The avalanche hurtles down the mountainside with terrifying speed, as if the entire mountain is spilling forth. Everywhere it passes, it paints an awe-inspiring yet dreadfully horrifying picture.
It was once the stuff of nightmares for the people of Kjerag, one that they could not flee fast enough from.
This time, however, a group of brave men and women stands firm at the mountain's foot, looking up with confidence.
With the wall of steel that they have built, they vow to challenge this snowy authority that has gone uncontested since time immemorial.
The tidal wave of ice and snow crashes against the line of defense formed by the trucks.
Despite being thousands of times heavier than man, the massive trucks seem insignificant before the power of nature and are pushed back. Some are even toppled.
But the wisdom of man prevails.
Gradually, the force pushing against the line of steel diminishes.
The defense line buckles, but it does not break, slowly coming to a stop a dozen meters before Weiss and the old man.
The avalanche, triggered by human hands, has been stopped.
When the new railroad is finished, it will carry this line of defense to every corner of Kjerag, ready to respond at a moment's notice.
Long has Kjeragandr's turnover been the terror of Kjerag. Many are the lives and homes it has taken.
But in the near future, the people of Kjerag will sit where you are now, watching our defense line stop avalanches, just as it did today.
Could you ever imagine something like this?
No, you couldn't.
Neither could I.
But it's happening before our eyes.
The old man's scarf has flown away in the wind, his hair and beard are caked with snow. Otherwise, he is completely unharmed.
Weiss continues to grab his shoulder with an iron hand, not giving him the slightest chance to escape.
But if he paid attention, the old noble would notice with a side glance that Weiss's attention is not on him at all.
His eyes are fixed on the line of steel that he has organized. His tightened grip on the old noble's shoulders is simply out of sheer excitement.
Degenbrecher?!

Shouldn't you be assisting with the evacuation?
Why are you coming down from the avalanche—
Wait, what's that on your back—?!
I heard there was a couple who weren't able to get out in time. I went to look for them.
They're alive.
Get them to a doctor, now.
Yes, sir. And ma'am!
I... Thank you so much, Degenbrecher.
So that's an avalanche. Interesting.
I'll be going. Feel free to call me when there's another one.
Will do.
She charged into that avalanche on her own?!
Honestly, I didn't expect it either.
But I hope you understand now.
The foreigners are given better treatment because they have what Kjerag doesn't, what Kjerag can't even imagine.
Think about it, Mr. Edwin.
Would you, or those behind you rather get swept away by the tide?
Or would you rather ride it and watch as we conquer what once seemed insurmountable?
Is it too late to get on board?
It's never too late.
Sir Enciodes welcomes everyone who is willing to build a new Kjerag together.
A moment of silence, then the old man nods, if only reluctantly.
I suppose I've grown old.
Not that old. Kjerag still needs you.
...I'll think about it. And I'll talk to them.
We're counting on it.
Weiss smiles.
The old man has seen Weiss smile many times. He knows that, more often than not, it is simply a form of self-defense.
But this time, it is sincere.
Sunlight dances on his face, and his smile is radiant.

recs.name: Run Like the Wind
recs.tag: O most nimble Itra in the mountains, are you prepared to descend into the vast unknown?

lines.x: Courier has a thick stack of paper in his hands as he stands by the shredder. The first page says 'Kjerag Logistics System Proposal'.
He wears a heavy, hesitant expression on his face, but eventually extends the proposal toward the shredder.
Wait.
Mr. Bison...
Why are you destroying the proposal?
Because it failed.
I'm your logistics lecturer. You're not the one who decides what's failed.
Besides, you didn't have that look on your face when you first told me you were drafting a proposal for Kjerag's logistics system.
May I have a look?
Yes, sir.
Pretty comprehensive.
You've covered all the bases, from manpower to cost to transportation method to storage.
It's a solid proposal.
There's only one problem left to solve—the engineering issues in Terra Nullius.
Right.
A Terra Nullius exists between the zone of actual Kjerag control and our neighboring countries.
A full-fledged logistics system requires a more developed transportation infrastructure, but neighboring countries will not simply sit and watch as Kjerag develops Terra Nullius.
I could not find a way to solve this problem, so I decided to give up.
If I recall correctly, I've discussed solutions to similar issues.
One way is to invest in an international logistics company.
In that case, there's no need to write a proposal at all—just leave it to a developed international logistics firm, like MountainDash Logistics.
We discussed this too.
In order to effectively operate in Kjerag, MountainDash would need someone reliable to manage local operations—someone like you.
But you refused. Do you regret that choice?
Well—no.
Another way is to leave Kjerag and establish my own logistics firm.
As clear as such a firm's Kjerag links would be, it would face a lot less opposition, as long as it does not belong to Kjerag officially.
I'm clear on that much, but—
You're not willing to accept it.
Just like you turned down my offer.
Because either way means leaving Karlan Trade, perhaps even leaving Kjerag.
It's the thought of leaving Kjerag that you really want to banish, isn't it?
I realized that everything in this proposal was written with the assumption that I would manage it personally.
The proposal was custom-made for myself. Implementing it means I'm the one who would need to leave Kjerag.
I was too arrogant.
So you're just giving up on the proposal?
I'll write a new one for the Master, so that he may find the right man.
So you're just giving up on the opportunity?
I know how much Kjerag means to you.
But this is a chance for you to show your value, isn't it?
If you're not interested—
Why did you choose to study at Rhodes Island?
Thank you for the kind words, but my mind is made up.
Courier snatches the proposal from Bison before he can react.
Before he can put the proposal in the shredder, however, he hears a crowing from behind him.
The fowlbeast is even faster than he, and whisks the proposal away in its beak. He is familiar with this fowlbeast—Tenzin.
...Master.
Your thoughts seem have been heading down a dangerous path lately.
I... I'm sorry, Master.
But—
But I'm also curious. Let's have you implement the proposal, Weiss.
Mapping, route planning, negotiating with the villages, deploying personnel...
Once you actually put things in place, you may find that they don't require your presence as much as you assumed they would.
Yes, Master.
Wait.
I'll go with you.
But—
You have an avalanche warning team, don't you?
Just treat me as one of them.
Let me see up close whether you really can do what you think you can.
Yes, Master.
Are you sure about this, Mr. SilverAsh?
I am.
It's high time Weiss took a good look at himself.
*Huff*... *huff*...
Here, take my hand, Master.
No need. What of the others?
They're already at the summit.
This trail may be a little difficult for you, sir.
You're just trying to get rid of me, aren't you, Weiss?
Of course not.
But one who spends his time in an office doing paperwork is bound to be less active than those of us who spend most of our time outdoors, no?
Heh.
We can take a break here.
The team at the summit can wait a while. They'll understand.
Let's go.
We can't delay the surveying on my account.
As you wish.
You're right, it has been a long time since I last climbed a hill.
You used to be very good at it.
I took after my mother.
Not so much these days.
You are still very much like her. You've just learned to hide it better.
By the way, I never told you this, but the day I took you in, I was only out there because my sisters made me go hunting with them.
I knew.
Did you?
Your sisters are not as tight-lipped as you are.
By chance, they had you join them on a hunting trip in the mountains that day. By chance, you got separated from them. By chance, you ran into me.
It was snowing heavily that day. You were lost too, weren't you?
You put on a brave face, told me to come with you, and took me to the Silverash manor.

When my grandparents came and begged the old master to take me on as a servant after I had lost my parents at a young age, it was you who persuaded him, saying that you wanted a male companion around your own age.
And so, I became part of Clan Silverash.
Perhaps...
Are your grandparents well?
Thanks to you, my grandfather is quite the man in Turicum's senior center, and my grandmother has opened a little shop of her own. They're rather enjoying their lives.
Good.
To me, Matterhorn is a guardian, one who has always served my family. I almost take him for granted. You're different.
You, I took under my own wing—at least, that's what I thought at the time.
Besides, you were quick and nimble. For a while, I had you carry my messages to others, and their messages back to me.
In truth, I was just trying to show you off.
There's no need to feel guilty about it.
It gave my life meaning.
After all, I was a wild child who popped suddenly into the family. My presence was unwelcome to many.
How can you be sure I did not use your name for my own designs in the process?
If you did, you hid it well.
Heh. How very you.
Besides—
At first, I did not enjoy running around the hills and mountains.
With time, however, as I walked the forests and the mountain trails—
As I climbed the snowy peaks—
As I breathed the air atop the peaks, and watched the spectacle of the mountains in the distance against the blue sky—
I felt happy.
I began to enjoy it.
Captain, Mast—SilverAsh. You're here.
Report.
We have good news and bad news.
Start with the good news.
This is the last location we're scheduled to visit on this survey trip. We've successfully plotted the Terra Nullius between Kjerag and our neighboring countries.
We have also located all the independent villages in Terra Nullius.
The experts have already plotted the most efficient and cost-effective route for transportation, assuming that the villages could be persuaded to act as hubs and depots.
And the bad news?
The bad news is... although plans for the route are essentially in place, and costs as well as time required are largely within acceptable boundaries...
Not all villages have accepted our proposal.
That's also to be expected. Which ones are they?
Take a look.
These few villages, especially this one.
They are not friendly to outsiders. The village headman, at least, seems reasonable, but opposition from the others puts him in an awkward position.

Wait, this village...
......
Pack it up.
Abandoning the plan?
No.
I'm going back to Turicum.
The key to persuading those villagers lies there.
Just to make sure I understand this correctly, Mr. Weiss... you need to persuade the villagers in order to establish a logistics route.
That's why you want me to write a letter to my father.
The villagers hold your father in high-esteem, after all.
Of course, we're not going to force you, if you're not willing.
I've already told you the potential risks, and the benefits.
Of course I'm willing!
If not for your recommendation, I would never have come to Kjerag, and I wouldn't have found this job.
Besides, it would be a dream come true if you really managed to establish such a route around Kjerag!
I'll get to it at once!
Wait.
Yes?
It's been a while since you've been home, hasn't it? If there's anything you want to send back to your family, I'll deliver it for you.
I-I couldn't trouble you with that.
It's no trouble. These villages on the frontier rarely get supplies from Kjerag.
Besides, it would improve the chances of swaying your father.
If you put it that way, I guess it would be rude to refuse.
You know the staff at Turicum Station well.
It's the main hub for all mail and cargo that goes through Kjerag.
I like it.
Is that why you chose to study logistics at Rhodes Island?
Yes.
I enjoy running through the mountains.
I enjoy seeing the expressions on faces when messages, letters, and packages are delivered.
Be it your face, or any others.
Be it expressions of joy, pain, or sorrow.
Maybe it all began with a childhood whim of yours—
But I began to enjoy the feeling.
The feeling of linking people together.
Besides...
At first, I didn't understand why you wouldn't give me and Matterhorn specific duties at Karlan Trade.
With time, however, I began to understand—
You wanted us to decide our own futures.
I never thought of myself as your master.
That's why I never thought about determining your fates for you.
But you never tell people what you think.
On this trip, I kept pondering why you wanted to tag along.
It didn't seem like something worth your time and effort, whether you meant to urge me to stay, or urge me to go.
Now, I'm beginning to understand.
Tell me more.
Now is not the time, not yet.
Perhaps you've forgotten—
But we've been to this village that we're about to visit before, more than a decade ago.
Yes?
Here's the letter, Mr. Weiss!
And this is the stuff to send to my folks.
It might be a little too much. If you don't think it works—
It's fine. Give them to this man here.
Wait, isn't that Sir Enciodes—
No, he's a member of the Kjerag Expedition, of which I am the captain.
...I see. I remember it now.
I'll take it.
H-Here you go, sir.
Ugh... it's heavy.
Who are you?
Have you forgotten me, Sage Edwards?
I am Weiss, captain of the Kjerag Expedition. This one here is Matterhorn, a warrior under my charge.
Ah, yes, I remember you.
Come and greet the sage, Matterhorn.
It's been a while, sir.
Very good, very good.
At first I thought you were hillmen coming from who-knows-where. Little could I imagine that you were heralds of Kjerag.
How is that son of mine, Chris, doing in Kjerag?
We came to deliver Chris's letter, sir.
Along with the gifts he prepared for his family.
So many things? My goodness. He shouldn't have.
(Softly) Whew—
(Whisper) Good work, Master.
(Whisper) Thanks.
Chris is doing very well in Kjerag. He is in line for a promotion to manager soon.
Please, go ahead and read the letter. It also explains why we're here.
I see. I know what you're here for.
Let's go inside.
May we count on you to convince the villagers, then?
It's no small business. There will be a lot to discuss.
But don't worry. With Chris's letter and your guarantee, I'm sure they'll come around.
Please feel free to let me know if our presence is warranted.
Very good, very good.
Do you remember now, Master?
Hard not to, after carrying so much all this way.
I wanted you to feel for yourself the importance of logistics.
Besides, I helped you carry half of it.
That day, I wanted to see what the outside was like, after my lessons.
